# Circuit quantile covers: variations without sharp-center assumptions

This strengthens all-active-circuit-directional-condition.md. For a
NECESSARY extremal condition, one does not need an exact derivative of actual
maximum depth. A family of exact circuit covers gives an upper comparison
function touching the depth at the original minimizer. This removes sharp
maximizers, unique center points, and finite representations of actual depth.

## 1. A local cap quantile exists because its anchor fiber is interior

Fix a positive-volume finite fiber family, and a cap

    H_j(b)={ (w,x): v_j.w+u_j.x>=b },       |u_j|=1,

whose boundary passes through an interior point of one of its fibers.
Allow the body to vary continuously with a finite parameter p, keeping all
fibers positive and bounded. Write F_j(p,b)=mu_p(H_j(b)).

For polytopal body deformations of the types used in the preceding notes,
F_j is locally Lipschitz in (p,b). This follows from an O(|delta p|)
Hausdorff bound, the corresponding boundary-neighborhood volume bound on a
finite uniformly bounded polytope family, and the slab bound for varying b.
A fixed ball in the anchor fiber supplies, for b in a neighborhood of b_j,
a uniform positive lower bound on its section area. Therefore F_j(p,b) is
uniformly strictly decreasing in b there. There are constants 0<c<C with

    c(b2-b1)<=F_j(p,b1)-F_j(p,b2)<=C(b2-b1)

for nearby b1<b2 and p. The upper bound is the uniform finite-fiber slab
bound. Consequently the equation

    F_j(p,Q_j(p,tau))=tau

has one nearby solution for (p,tau) near the base pair. Q_j is locally
Lipschitz and strictly decreasing in tau. Boundary coincidences in other
fibers do not impair this strict monotonicity.

## 2. An exact common-mass circuit cover at every nearby body

Fix ANY positive active circuit at the restricted depth maximum in integer
fiber z. Its caps have the same base unnormalized mass tau0 and satisfy

    sum_j rho_j u_j=0, rho_j>0, sum_j rho_j=1,
    sum_j rho_j b_j=A.z,      A=sum_j rho_j v_j.

Keep all ambient normals fixed. Define tau_c(p) as the unique nearby root

    sum_j rho_j Q_j(p,tau_c(p))=A.z.                                (1)

Existence, uniqueness and continuity follow from the preceding uniform
strict monotonicity. The adjusted closed caps

    H_j(Q_j(p,tau_c(p)))

all have EXACT mass tau_c(p). Their weighted margins on the entire fiber
over z sum to zero. Hence at least one margin is nonnegative at every point
of that full continuous fiber. They are an exact closed cover of {z}xR^d.
In particular the new restricted maximum depth is at most tau_c(p)/M(p).
No selected or moved center is needed for this statement.

Select any one active circuit for EVERY integer index, using the known
local critical circuits. Their quantile covers together cover P x R^d.
At the base, the selected circuits from globally deepest fibers have mass
beta M; every other selected circuit has a strict mass gap. Thus, near an
attained depth minimizer, these exact comparison covers give

    maximum depth at p <= max_(z deepest) tau_cz(p)/M(p),            (2)

after shrinking the neighborhood to keep all nondeep circuit roots below
the right side. The comparison agrees with beta at the original body.
The selection of a circuit at each deepest fiber is completely arbitrary.

## 3. The smooth consequence has no sharpness or finite-depth-model gap

When the relevant cap cuts are smooth and transverse, let B_j(delta) be the
body-shape derivative of their mass at fixed threshold, and let S_j>0 be
the total section area. Implicit differentiation gives

    Q_j'(delta,a)=(B_j(delta)-a)/S_j.

Differentiating (1) yields exactly

    tau_c'(delta)=[sum_j rho_j B_j(delta)/S_j]/[sum_j rho_j/S_j].      (3)

At an attained local depth minimum, (2) implies for every admissible delta
and EVERY selection of active circuits, one at each deepest index,

    max_z [tau_cz'(delta)-beta M'(delta)]>=0.                        (4)

Thus the robust rainbow necessary condition in the preceding note holds
for actual mixed-integer depth under smooth shape/cap derivatives, without
assuming any isolated or sharp center and without assuming finitely many
active ambient halfspaces. Only a finite selected circuit is used at a time.
For open body parameters, each arbitrary rainbow selection of the linear
functionals in (3), after subtracting beta M', must have zero in its convex
hull. With one deepest fiber EVERY active circuit functional equals beta M'
on the full parameter space.

One may replace each fiber's circuit functionals by their convex hull: if a
convexified rainbow selection were strictly negative in some direction,
then at each color at least one original functional in its convex mixture
would be negative, contradicting (4). Closure is harmless by continuity and
strict separation. Consequently the contributor's robust-circuit-gradient-rank
lemma applies to these convexified families whenever the stated smooth
first-order derivatives exist.

## 4. Coincident cap boundaries have an exact directional inverse

The same construction survives nonsmooth cap coincidences. Suppose the
body deformation has a Hadamard directional mass derivative

    D_j(delta,s)=F_j'((p0,b_j);(delta,s)).

This holds for the finite support/facet and shared-plane deformations in the
previous notes, by their swept-prism formulas. Normalize u_j to unit length.
On an ordinary proper section the threshold contribution is -s times its
area. At a coincident body facet, with actual outward body velocity r(x),
the local contributions are

    min(r(x),-s)             if the original body lies inside the cap,
    max(r(x)-s,0)            if the original body lies outside the cap.

If several body planes own the facet, r(x) is their minimum velocity.
Integrate these contributions and add the ordinary noncoincident terms.
They give a continuous positively homogeneous function D_j(delta,s).
When rotations occur, the affine r(x) can change its active branch within
a facet; no constant whole-facet trace is being assumed.

The anchor's proper section contributes a fixed strictly negative slope
in s. All other terms are nonincreasing in s. Uniform slab bounds give the
opposite Lipschitz bound. Thus for every delta and a there is a unique
q_j(delta,a) satisfying

    D_j(delta,q_j(delta,a))=a.                                     (5)

It depends continuously on (delta,a), is positively homogeneous, and is
strictly decreasing in a. The local quantile has Hadamard derivative
Q_j'(delta,a)=q_j(delta,a). Indeed the Lipschitz quantile estimate first
bounds the difference quotient; every convergent subsequence must solve
(5) by the directional expansion, and uniqueness identifies its limit.
The same argument is uniform for convergent directions, giving the Hadamard
rather than merely ray derivative.

Equation (1) therefore has the unique directional derivative a_c(delta)
characterized by

    sum_j rho_j q_j(delta,a_c(delta))=0.                            (6)

It is continuous and positively homogeneous. This proves the exact
nonsmooth form of (4):

    for every selected active circuit at each deepest index,
    max_z [a_cz(delta)-beta M'(delta)]>=0.                          (7)

This remains valid if the total-volume derivative is also nonsmooth from
shared body-plane owner ties. Equation (7) is a proved directional necessary
condition, with all cap-boundary mass effects retained. In that case it is
not justified to replace its nonlinear homogeneous terms by one convenient
linear stress or to apply a linear rank lemma without an additional argument.

For fixed fiber support-fan deformations, all facet velocities are constant
on each facet, so the formulas involve finitely many minima/maxima of linear
forms and the circuit root is piecewise linear in the direction. General
shared-plane rotations require the full integrated formulas above.

No claimed per-group numerical bound follows merely from these conditions.
